# ADR: Autogenerated numeric card codes

**Date**: 2026-08-06
**Status**: accepted
**Modules affected**: cards, infrastructure

## Context

Every card required a `code` typed by the operator, but most cards are issued without a
pre-printed number — the operator was inventing one, which is slow and collides. The code
is `TEXT`, unique per `(tenant_id, code)`, and must stay a string end to end: a 5-digit
code includes `"00042"`, so any integer round trip silently destroys it. The obvious
implementation — SELECT to check availability, then INSERT — is racy and pointless here:
the Neon HTTP driver has no interactive transactions, so the two statements cannot be
atomic (`foundation/04-constraints.md` #13). Uniqueness therefore has to be arbitrated by
the existing unique index, which means reacting to a driver-level 23505 rather than
predicting it. A generated code also has to coexist with manual entry, which stays
untouched: a manual code may come off a pre-existing physical card and can be any charset.

## Decision

When `createCard` receives no code (absent or blank) it allocates one by generating random
decimal digits and attempting the insert, retrying on a `(tenant_id, code)` unique
violation; the length starts at 5 digits and grows one digit at a time, per code, only for
the card currently being created. Uniqueness is decided exclusively by the
`cards_tenant_code_unique` index — there is no pre-check SELECT on the generated path.
The create form offers an "assign automatically" switch, on by default, and submits no
code when it is on.

## Consequences

- **Positive:** operators create cards without inventing identifiers; codes are unique by
  construction under concurrency, with no lock, no counter row, and no extra round trip in
  the common case (first candidate wins). The manual path is byte-for-byte unchanged, so
  pre-printed cards keep working. The policy lives in three constants and nothing
  persisted depends on it, so it can be retuned without a migration or a backfill.
- **Negative / trade-offs:** codes of different lengths coexist in one tenant, which looks
  inconsistent in a list. Retries cost extra round trips, bounded at 8 per length. The
  retry hinges on matching a driver error by SQLSTATE **and** constraint name, so renaming
  the index without updating `CARDS_TENANT_CODE_UNIQUE` would turn a collision into a hard
  failure — the constant is exported from the schema and used by `unique()` itself to keep
  the two from drifting.
- **Follow-ups:** per-card-type code formats (prefixes, checksums, fixed width) are
  deliberately deferred — no `code_generation` column was added. `isUniqueViolation` is now
  available for any other insert that wants the index to arbitrate instead of a pre-check.

## Alternatives considered

- **Per-tenant counter column / Postgres sequence** — gives short, gapless, guessable
  codes, but needs a persisted length or counter, a migration, and a read-modify-write that
  is exactly the atomicity this driver cannot provide.
- **Pre-check SELECT then INSERT** — the intuitive version, rejected: without interactive
  transactions it is a race with a wider window than doing nothing, and the unique index
  has to be handled anyway.
- **UUID / nanoid-derived codes** — unique without coordination, but non-numeric and far
  too long to read off a badge or type into the scanner fallback.
- **A fixed length with no growth** — simpler, but has no escape hatch if a tenant ever
  saturates the keyspace; the adaptive step costs one comparison and never triggers at this
  product's scale.
